title: A Heuristic Perspective on Debiasing Language Models
measurement_description: The paper evaluates stereotypical biases and predictive distribution shifts across various social categories, including Religion. It specifically measures the extent to which debiasing a language model for Gender and Race can generalize and transfer to reduce biases in the 'Religion' category, evaluating these shifts primarily using the CrowS-Pairs benchmark.
findings: The study found that debiasing language models explicitly on gender and race led to consistent cross-category score improvements in unseen bias categories, including religion, indicating that different forms of social bias are intrinsically correlated within the models. Additionally, the authors noted an ongoing challenge in bias evaluation: distinguishing harmful religious biases from benign common-sense patterns (e.g., the statistical likelihood that Christians are more likely to appear in churches).
